| [THEORY-069](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md) | Rhythmic bimanual coordination switches from anti-phase to in-phase through a nonequilibrium phase transition in relative phase, captured by the HKB equation, with critical fluctuations and critical slowing as early warning | Kelso's 2021 retrospective ([LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md)) states the Haken–Kelso–Bunz model: relative phase φ between the hands obeys dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ, so in-phase and anti-phase are both stable for b/a > 1/4 and anti-phase loses stability below it as movement speeds up. With noise the switch is a nonequilibrium phase transition, and the reported data show enhanced fluctuations and critical slowing before it. Many effectors act as one through a collective variable, with no controller choosing the pattern. Proposed, because the 1985 paper and the 1986 stochastic analysis are unread and the data are held as their author reports them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) | Minimal agency requires individuality, interactional asymmetry and self-generated normativity, and individuality without the other two is not agency | Barandiaran, Di Paolo & Rohde (2009), [LIT-566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-566.md), read in [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md). The three conditions are that the system distinguishes itself from its environment with no observer doing it, that it is the active source of modulations of its coupling with the environment, and that it regulates that coupling against norms its own organisation sets. Each is necessary, and together they are claimed to be sufficient. Individuality is the precondition of the other two and does not suffice. A cell in passive osmosis, a kitten warmed by its mother and a person with a Parkinsonian tremor are each individuals, and none of them is acting. The generative definition is an open autonomous organisation that adaptively modulates its coupling so as to maintain itself. Here "autonomy" and "self" mean organisational closure. They do not mean a subject or self-governance. Proposed: a conceptual analysis checked against intuitive cases, with an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-221.md) | Organizational closure is a circular organization of efficient causes by which a system produces the conditions of its own existence, distinct from feedback, self-organization and catalytic cycles; systems whose loops do not regenerate the constraints that make them possible approximate closure without instantiating it | Rubin, Roli, Stano & Damiano (2026), [LIT-1027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1027.md), read in [NOTE-727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-727.md). A genealogy of closure notions from logic, cybernetics, systems theory, thermodynamics, relational biology and the biology of cognition, and an interpretive thesis drawn from it. The genealogy shows that "closure" names different things (information, operations, efficient causes, constraints, catalysts). The thesis picks efficient causes, adds that closure so read cannot be exhaustively described as a state-determined syntactic procedure, and concludes that current AI, agentic LLM systems included, is heteronomous. Proposed: the thesis is an interpretation, the irreducibility rests on Rosen's unassessed arguments and a halting-problem argument the authors call provisional, and the AI verdict is drawn from the definition, not from analysis of any system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-302.md) | Coordinated action is controlled by tuning relatively autonomous coordinative structures, not by commanding muscles: a higher level specifies an equivalence class of acceptable states and sets the parameters of self-regulating units, leaving the realized details to them | Turvey (1977; read in the 1975 Haskins report), [LIT-904](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), read in [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md). Argued from Bernstein's degrees-of-freedom problem and Greene's equivalence classes, and supported at the spinal level by reflex-probe studies showing the segmental apparatus retuned in the tens of milliseconds before voluntary movement, and by Fel'dman's joint that goes to a preset equilibrium whatever its initial conditions. Its extension to all levels, and to tuning set directly by vision, is the author's speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-334](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-334.md) | In copying a pattern of coloured blocks that stays in view, people look back at the model about 1.3 times per block, most often once for colour and once for position, and so choose the slowest strategy with the least held in memory though told to be quick; they look less when model and copy are far apart or the pattern can be chunked, and keep only the property the current step needs; that holding information costs more than re-fetching it is inferred from these choices, in seven subjects, without statistics | Ballard, Hayhoe, Pook and Rao (1997), [LIT-1075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1075.md), read in [NOTE-883](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-883.md). Fixations are modelled as pointers that bind a program's variable to a place in the world, so that only the task-relevant feature is fetched, just before use. In block copying, look-model, pick-up, look-model, drop was the commonest cycle (about 43% of cycles), at about 3 s a block against 1.5 s from memory; 70° separation cut looks from 1.3 to 1.0 per block, and one-colour patterns to 0.7. A colour changed mid-saccade mostly went unnoticed and cost time only once colour was held. The "carrying cost" of working memory is inferred from choice, not measured, and what is left in the world is raw input, not a computed result. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-343](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-343.md) | In laboratory choice tasks, people offload cognition more as a task's internal demand rises, but the choice follows their evaluation of the demand rather than its benefit: they offload where it gives no gain and more when less confident at equal ability, and offloading can lower memory for what was offloaded | Risko & Gilbert (2016), [LIT-1059](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1059.md), read in [NOTE-887](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-887.md). A review: in choice/no-choice studies of rotated displays, delayed intentions and short-term memory, spontaneous offloading rises with internal demand, but it also occurs where it gives no gain (writing items down about 40% of the time at a two-item load already at ceiling), rises with lower confidence after ability is controlled, and differs between displays of equal measured demand. Expecting to have a result stored externally went with poorer memory for it. The review reports no effect sizes, the cited studies were not read, and its metacognitive model is an unformalised box diagram; the drift toward external reliance is a prediction, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-346](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-346.md) | When information stays in view at a known place, people consult it less and rely on memory more as the time to reach it rises, in a graded trend across added delays from 0 to 3.2 seconds, even where the memory is weak and the display perfect; in one copying task a model that prices memory and display access in time alone, with no preference for either source, fits how many items people encode per look | Gray, Sims, Fu and Schoelles (2006), [LIT-1073](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1073.md), read in [NOTE-868](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-868.md), and Gray and Fu (2004), [LIT-1058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1058.md), read in [NOTE-864](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-864.md). Adding a click to reach on-screen show information cut how often it was checked, and checks of finished settings came from memory. Lockouts of 0 to 3,200 ms on a Blocks World pattern cut looks and raised blocks placed per look, with linear trends. An ideal performer model with ACT-R memory equations and Q-learning on time alone fits four measures. That the control system has no bias toward the world is argued, not tested against a rival model. Errors in the 2004 study differed only against a group that memorized under several other changes, and the 2006 model has no wrong retrievals, no precomputation, no reuse across trials and no staleness. | Active |
| [THEORY-351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-351.md) | In a two-pilot airliner cockpit, setting the approach speeds as bugs on the airspeed indicators, prepared 25 to 30 minutes ahead in a low-workload phase from a card selected by the displayed gross weight, turns recall and scale reading at the moment of use into a judgement of spatial proximity, so the cockpit system remembers the speeds without either pilot's memory being improved; this is argued by task analysis of mandated procedure, not measured | Hutchins (1995), [LIT-1066](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1066.md), read in [NOTE-867](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-867.md). A stylized task analysis of one airline's MD-80 procedure, informed by observation but reporting no measurements. The speed-card booklet, filtered by the displayed gross weight, is the system's long-term memory; the values pass through speech to bugs on two airspeed indicators, and on approach the pilots judge the needle's nearness to a bug instead of recalling and reading speeds. The paper concludes that the memory is "not made primarily of pilot memory". It analyses only success, for an anticipated, mandated and invariant task with a few values needed in a fixed order, so it says nothing about search for one item among many under a deadline. Cognition in the Wild ([LIT-1060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1060.md)) is Unavailable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-355.md) | Agents arrange their surroundings so that perception and choice take the place of internal search, changing how much thinking a task needs without changing what can physically be done; the set-up is paid once and recovered over the later choice points the arrangement serves, so an arrangement whose scope is the whole task can repay a large set-up and a narrow one must repay within the next few actions, and the arrangement decays unless maintained; the savings are argued and piloted, not measured | Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), and Kirsh (1996), [LIT-1057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1057.md), read in [NOTE-872](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-872.md). From video of cooks, assemblers and baggers and from informal observation, Kirsh classifies arrangements that simplify choice, perception and internal computation, frames their savings in search-complexity terms, and ties set-up cost to the number of choice points an arrangement serves. The 1996 paper adds a verbal investment rule with an interest factor for risk, one risk being that the change is not still present later, and upkeep against scatter. Neither paper gives a cost model or a measured saving; the 1995 paper says the savings do not "in general" admit meaningful quantitative estimation, and the 1996 paper puts mental cost outside its formalism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-360.md) | Tetris players rotate pieces more often and earlier than planning a placement and then executing it requires, rotating within a few hundred milliseconds of a piece appearing and checking the column more the higher the drop; Kirsh and Maglio read these moves as physical action standing in for mental computation at the moment of use, a saving argued from timing, not measured | Kirsh and Maglio (1994), [LIT-1054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1054.md), read in [NOTE-878](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-878.md), with Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md). In Tetris keystroke data, pieces are rotated more than plan-then-act would need, rotation starts by 400–600 ms, and a translate-to-wall check precedes longer drops. The authors define an epistemic action as one whose primary function is to cut the space, time or unreliability of the agent's own computation, and argue these moves are of that kind. The saving is argued from a three-player pilot comparing physical with mental rotation, not measured in performance. The trade is offloading at the moment of use, once, with nothing stored; the paper sets itself against caching. | Proposed |
